item.statement: Hoeffding tail bound for averages of variables in [-1,1]

chk.evidence: Bib metadata checked with Crossref (https://api.crossref.org/works/10.1080/01621459.1963.10500830): "Probability Inequalities for Sums of Bounded Random Variables", Wassily Hoeffding, Journal of the American Statistical Association 58(301):13-30, March 1963. The refs.bib entry matches exactly. The tandfonline DOI page returned 403. The scanned PDF mirror (userpages.cs.umbc.edu) had no text layer, so I have no verbatim quote. The standard statement of Hoeffding 1963 Thm 2 is: for independent a_i <= X_i <= b_i, P(Xbar - E Xbar >= t) <= exp(-2n^2 t^2 / sum(b_i-a_i)^2). I checked the paper's use of it (appendix.tex:189): X_l = cos(2 pi J_l delta/p) in [-1,1], i.i.d. J_l, mean -1/(p-1), so t > 1/2 and the bound is exp(-L t^2/2) <= e^{-L/8} <= 1/p for L = ceil(8 ln p). The union bound over p-1 offsets gives failure probability < 1. All correct. Notes: /Users/ruhaanrajadhyaksha/projects/grok/heracles/paper/litcheck/items/c13-hoeffding/CHECK.md

recommended_citations.why: Supports the tail bound in app:scaling (Thm 2: bounded independent summands). Metadata confirmed via Crossref.
